task: Write the canonical Dynamic Finding System execution plan that turns seven historically evidenced Finding failure classes into a safe four-component architecture and three bounded implementation Stories.
outcome: The user opens one Markdown plan and can see, for every one of the seven problems, the evidence that proves it, the component that owns it, the exact follow-up Story that delivers it, the dependency order, the gate behavior, and the acceptance test; the document also explains why @lattice/lab changes from historically out of scope to currently applicable without changing the package in this Story.
facts: The exact component names are Finding Ledger Integrity; Candidate and Defect Identity; Dynamic Applicability; and Freshness and Supersession.
The exact follow-up Story names are Dynamic Finding Applicability; Finding Identity and Historical Lineage; and Finding Ledger and Runtime Evidence Integrity.
The current Finding gate consumes status, severity, evidenceState, and round policy, but no current-Story applicability verdict.

Historical CLI evidence includes B-cdf6:F-056 runtime-artifact false positive, B-cdf6:F-067 verified pre-existing routing, B-cdf6:F-070 detector noise, and B-META-framework-audit:F-029/F-031 ledger and correction failures.
Historical learning remains non-authoritative and cannot itself satisfy lifecycle gates.
The package rename from @lattice/lab to @proof-or-stop/lab is an example only; implementation remains out of scope.
constraints: Write repository artifacts in English and create only one canonical Markdown decision document.
Do not directly read or edit protected Story or fixture storage.
Do not implement runtime schemas, gates, package renames, or create the three follow-up Stories.
Label corpus counts as a dated, HEAD-bound observation and provide regeneration commands because the values drift.
Treat applicability as a new gate-consumed process fact only after current signed evidence; never let historical learning directly block or unblock.
Distinguish historical incidents from claims that the same defect remains unresolved in current code.
